questions.text: Let $A=\{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 10\}$ and $B=\left\{\dfrac{m}{n}: m, n\in A, m<n \text{ and } \gcd(m, n)=1\right\}$. Then $n(B)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
For each denominator $n$ ($2\le n\le10$), the admissible numerators are the $m<n$ coprime to $n$, i.e. $\varphi(n)$ of them, and different reduced fractions are different numbers.
$n(B)=\varphi(2)+\cdots+\varphi(10)=1+2+2+4+2+6+4+6+4=31$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The number of non-empty equivalence relations on the set $\{1, 2, 3\}$ is :
questions.sol:
Equivalence relations on a set correspond one-to-one with its partitions.
Partitions of $\{1,2,3\}$: one block (1 way), a pair and a singleton (3 ways), three singletons (1 way).
Total $=5$ (every equivalence relation on a non-empty set is non-empty).

questions.text: The product of all solutions of the equation $e^{5(\log_e x)^2+3}=x^8$, $x>0$, is :
questions.sol:
Take natural logarithms and put $t=\log_e x$: $5t^2+3=8t$, i.e. $5t^2-8t+3=0$.
Sum of the roots $t_1+t_2=\dfrac85$.
Product of the solutions $x_1x_2=e^{t_1+t_2}=e^{8/5}$.

questions.text: Let $z_1$, $z_2$ and $z_3$ be three complex numbers on the circle $|z|=1$ with $\arg(z_1)=\dfrac{-\pi}{4}$, $\arg(z_2)=0$ and $\arg(z_3)=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$. If $\left|z_1\bar{z}_2+z_2\bar{z}_3+z_3\bar{z}_1\right|^2=\alpha+\beta\sqrt{2}$, $\alpha, \beta\in\mathbf{Z}$, then the value of $\alpha^2+\beta^2$ is :
questions.sol:
$z_1\bar z_2=e^{-i\pi/4}$, $z_2\bar z_3=e^{-i\pi/4}$, $z_3\bar z_1=e^{i\pi/2}=i$.
Sum $=2e^{-i\pi/4}+i=\sqrt2+i(1-\sqrt2)$.
Modulus squared $=2+(1-\sqrt2)^2=5-2\sqrt2$, so $\alpha=5$, $\beta=-2$.
$\alpha^2+\beta^2=29$.

questions.text: If $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{n}T_r=\frac{(2n-1)(2n+1)(2n+3)(2n+5)}{64}$, then $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{r=1}^{n}\left(\frac{1}{T_r}\right)$ is equal to :
questions.note: Strictly, the given sum formula does not vanish at $n=0$, so $T_1=\dfrac{105}{64}$ rather than $\dfrac{15}{8}$, and the limit would then be $\dfrac{26}{35}$, which is not an option. NTA's final key gives $\dfrac23$, the value obtained by using $T_r=\dfrac{(2r-1)(2r+1)(2r+3)}{8}$ for every $r$.
questions.sol:
$T_r=S_r-S_{r-1}=\dfrac{(2r-1)(2r+1)(2r+3)}{64}\left[(2r+5)-(2r-3)\right]=\dfrac{(2r-1)(2r+1)(2r+3)}{8}$.
$\dfrac{1}{(2r-1)(2r+1)(2r+3)}=\dfrac14\left[\dfrac{1}{(2r-1)(2r+1)}-\dfrac{1}{(2r+1)(2r+3)}\right]$, which telescopes.
$\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{\infty}\frac1{T_r}=8\cdot\frac14\cdot\frac{1}{1\cdot3}=\frac23$.

questions.text: Let $a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots$ be a G.P. of increasing positive terms. If $a_1a_5=28$ and $a_2+a_4=29$, then $a_6$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$a_2a_4=a_1a_5=28$ and $a_2+a_4=29$, so $a_2, a_4$ are 1 and 28; increasing terms give $a_2=1$, $a_4=28$.
Then $r^2=28$ and $a_6=a_4r^2=28\times28=784$.

questions.text: From all the English alphabets, five letters are chosen and are arranged in alphabetical order. The total number of ways, in which the middle letter is 'M', is :
questions.sol:
M is the 13th letter: 12 letters come before it and 13 after it.
Choose 2 letters from the 12 before and 2 from the 13 after; the alphabetical arrangement is then fixed.
Number of ways $=\binom{12}{2}\binom{13}{2}=66\times78=5148$.

questions.text: A coin is tossed three times. Let X denote the number of times a tail follows a head. If $\mu$ and $\sigma^2$ denote the mean and variance of X, then the value of $64(\mu+\sigma^2)$ is :
questions.sol:
X counts the occurrences of "HT" in the sequence. HHT, HTH, HTT and THT give $X=1$; HHH, THH, TTH and TTT give $X=0$ (two HT's cannot fit in three tosses).
So $P(X=1)=\dfrac12$: $\mu=\dfrac12$, $\sigma^2=\dfrac12-\dfrac14=\dfrac14$.
$64(\mu+\sigma^2)=64\times\dfrac34=48$.

questions.text: Two balls are selected at random one by one without replacement from a bag containing 4 white and 6 black balls. If the probability that the first selected ball is black, given that the second selected ball is also black, is $\dfrac{m}{n}$, where $\gcd(m, n)=1$, then $m+n$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$P(B_1\cap B_2)=\dfrac{6}{10}\cdot\dfrac59=\dfrac13$ and $P(B_2)=P(B_1)=\dfrac35$ (by symmetry).
$P(B_1\mid B_2)=\dfrac{1/3}{3/5}=\dfrac59$, so $m+n=14$.

questions.text: Let the triangle PQR be the image of the triangle with vertices $(1, 3)$, $(3, 1)$ and $(2, 4)$ in the line $x+2y=2$. If the centroid of $\Delta$PQR is the point $(\alpha, \beta)$, then $15(\alpha-\beta)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Reflection preserves centroids, so reflect the centroid $G\left(2, \dfrac83\right)$ of the original triangle.
$x+2y-2$ at $G$ equals $\dfrac{16}{3}$; the image is $G-\dfrac{2(16/3)}{5}(1, 2)=\left(2-\dfrac{32}{15}, \dfrac83-\dfrac{64}{15}\right)=\left(-\dfrac{2}{15}, -\dfrac{24}{15}\right)$.
$15(\alpha-\beta)=-2+24=22$.

questions.text: A circle C of radius 2 lies in the second quadrant and touches both the coordinate axes. Let r be the radius of a circle that has centre at the point $(2, 5)$ and intersects the circle C at exactly two points. If the set of all possible values of r is the interval $(\alpha, \beta)$, then $3\beta-2\alpha$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
C has centre $(-2, 2)$ and radius 2. Distance between the centres $=\sqrt{16+9}=5$.
Two intersection points need $|r-2|<5<r+2$, i.e. $3<r<7$.
$3\beta-2\alpha=21-6=15$.

questions.text: Let the parabola $y=x^2+px-3$, meet the coordinate axes at the points P, Q and R. If the circle C with centre at $(-1, -1)$ passes through the points P, Q and R, then the area of $\Delta$PQR is :
questions.sol:
The parabola meets the $y$-axis at $(0, -3)$, so the radius$^2$ of C is $1+4=5$.
C meets the $x$-axis where $(x+1)^2+1=5$: $x=1, -3$. These are the roots of $x^2+px-3=0$ (product $-3$), so $p=2$.
Area of the triangle with vertices $(1, 0)$, $(-3, 0)$, $(0, -3)$ $=\dfrac12\times4\times3=6$.

questions.text: Let the foci of a hyperbola be $(1, 14)$ and $(1, -12)$. If it passes through the point $(1, 6)$, then the length of its latus-rectum is :
questions.sol:
Centre $(1, 1)$, $c=13$, transverse axis along $x=1$.
$(1, 6)$ lies on the transverse axis, so it is a vertex: $a=5$.
$b^2=c^2-a^2=144$; latus rectum $=\dfrac{2b^2}{a}=\dfrac{288}{5}$.

questions.text: Using the principal values of the inverse trigonometric functions, the sum of the maximum and the minimum values of $16\left(\left(\sec^{-1}x\right)^2+\left(\operatorname{cosec}^{-1}x\right)^2\right)$ is :
questions.sol:
For $|x|\ge1$, $\operatorname{cosec}^{-1}x=\dfrac\pi2-\sec^{-1}x$. Let $\theta=\sec^{-1}x\in[0, \pi]$, $\theta\ne\dfrac\pi2$.
$g(\theta)=\theta^2+\left(\dfrac\pi2-\theta\right)^2$ has its minimum $\dfrac{\pi^2}{8}$ at $\theta=\dfrac\pi4$ and its maximum $\pi^2+\dfrac{\pi^2}{4}=\dfrac{5\pi^2}{4}$ at $\theta=\pi$.
$16\left(\dfrac{\pi^2}{8}+\dfrac{5\pi^2}{4}\right)=2\pi^2+20\pi^2=22\pi^2$.

questions.text: Let $L_1:\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y-2}{3}=\dfrac{z-3}{4}$ and $L_2:\dfrac{x-2}{3}=\dfrac{y-4}{4}=\dfrac{z-5}{5}$ be two lines. Then which of the following points lies on the line of the shortest distance between $L_1$ and $L_2$ ?
questions.sol:
Common perpendicular direction: $(2,3,4)\times(3,4,5)=(-1, 2, -1)$.
Take $P(1+2s, 2+3s, 3+4s)$ on $L_1$ and $Q(2+3t, 4+4t, 5+5t)$ on $L_2$; $\vec{PQ}\perp$ both lines gives $16+38t-29s=0$ and $21+50t-38s=0$, so $t=-\dfrac16$, $s=\dfrac13$.
$P=\left(\dfrac53, 3, \dfrac{13}{3}\right)$; the line is $\left(\dfrac53, 3, \dfrac{13}{3}\right)+k(-1, 2, -1)$.
$k=-3$ gives $\left(\dfrac{14}{3}, -3, \dfrac{22}{3}\right)$.

questions.text: Let $f:\mathbf{R}\to\mathbf{R}$ be a twice differentiable function such that $f(x+y)=f(x)f(y)$ for all $x, y\in\mathbf{R}$. If $f'(0)=4a$ and $f$ satisfies $f''(x)-3af'(x)-f(x)=0$, $a>0$, then the area of the region $R=\{(x, y)\mid 0\le y\le f(ax), 0\le x\le 2\}$ is :
questions.sol:
A differentiable non-zero solution of $f(x+y)=f(x)f(y)$ is $f(x)=e^{kx}$ with $k=f'(0)=4a$.
Then $k^2-3ak-1=0$: $16a^2-12a^2=1$, so $a=\dfrac12$, $k=2$ and $f(ax)=e^{x}$.
Area $=\displaystyle\int_0^2 e^x\,dx=e^2-1$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let for $f(x)=7\tan^8x+7\tan^6x-3\tan^4x-3\tan^2x$, $I_1=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}f(x)\,dx$ and $I_2=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}x f(x)\,dx$. Then $7I_1+12I_2$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$f(x)=(7\tan^6x-3\tan^2x)\sec^2x=\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\tan^7x-\tan^3x\right)$.
$I_1=\left[\tan^7x-\tan^3x\right]_0^{\pi/4}=0$.
By parts, $I_2=\left[x(\tan^7x-\tan^3x)\right]_0^{\pi/4}-\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\tan^3x(\tan^2x-1)\sec^2x\,dx=0-\int_0^1(u^5-u^3)\,du=\frac1{12}$.
$7I_1+12I_2=1$.

questions.text: The area of the region, inside the circle $\left(x-2\sqrt{3}\right)^2+y^2=12$ and outside the parabola $y^2=2\sqrt{3}x$ is :
questions.sol:
The curves meet at $x=0$ and $x=2\sqrt3$ (points $(2\sqrt3, \pm2\sqrt3)$, the ends of the vertical diameter). For $0<x<2\sqrt3$ the parabola lies inside the circle.
Region inside both $=$ right half-disc $6\pi$ $+$ $\displaystyle\int_0^{2\sqrt3}2\sqrt{2\sqrt3\,x}\,dx=6\pi+16$.
Required area $=12\pi-(6\pi+16)=6\pi-16$.

questions.text: Let $x=x(y)$ be the solution of the differential equation $y^2dx+\left(x-\dfrac{1}{y}\right)dy=0$. If $x(1)=1$, then $x\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$ is :
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{dx}{dy}+\dfrac{x}{y^2}=\dfrac1{y^3}$; integrating factor $e^{-1/y}$.
With $t=\dfrac1y$: $xe^{-1/y}=\displaystyle\int\frac{e^{-1/y}}{y^3}dy=(t+1)e^{-t}+C$, so $x=\dfrac1y+1+Ce^{1/y}$.
$x(1)=1$: $C=-\dfrac1e$. Then $x\left(\dfrac12\right)=2+1-\dfrac{e^2}{e}=3-e$.

questions.text: Let A be a square matrix of order 3 such that $\det(A)=-2$ and $\det\left(3\operatorname{adj}\left(-6\operatorname{adj}(3A)\right)\right)=2^{m+n}\cdot3^{mn}$, $m>n$. Then $4m+2n$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
For order 3: $\operatorname{adj}(kM)=k^2\operatorname{adj}M$ and $\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}A)=(\det A)A=-2A$.
$\operatorname{adj}(3A)=9\operatorname{adj}A$; $\operatorname{adj}(-54\operatorname{adj}A)=54^2(-2A)$.
$3\cdot54^2\cdot(-2)A=-17496A$ and $17496=2^3\cdot3^7$.
$\det=(-17496)^3(-2)=2^{10}\cdot3^{21}$, so $m+n=10$, $mn=21$: $m=7$, $n=3$.
$4m+2n=34$.

questions.text: Let $\vec{c}$ be the projection vector of $\vec{b}=\lambda\hat{i}+4\hat{k}$, $\lambda>0$, on the vector $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$. If $|\vec{a}+\vec{c}|=7$, then the area of the parallelogram formed by the vectors $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ is __________.
questions.sol:
$\vec c=\dfrac{\vec b\cdot\vec a}{|\vec a|^2}\vec a=\dfrac{\lambda+8}{9}\vec a$, so $|\vec a+\vec c|=3\left(1+\dfrac{\lambda+8}{9}\right)=7$, giving $\lambda=4$ and $\vec c=\dfrac43(1, 2, 2)$.
$\vec b\times\vec c=\dfrac43(4, 0, 4)\times(1, 2, 2)=\dfrac43(-8, -4, 8)$, of magnitude $\dfrac43\times12=16$.

questions.text: Let the function, $f(x)=\begin{cases}-3ax^2-2, & x<1\\ a^2+bx, & x\ge1\end{cases}$ be differentiable for all $x\in\mathbf{R}$, where $a>1$, $b\in\mathbf{R}$. If the area of the region enclosed by $y=f(x)$ and the line $y=-20$ is $\alpha+\beta\sqrt{3}$, $\alpha, \beta\in\mathbf{Z}$, then the value of $\alpha+\beta$ is __________.
questions.sol:
Differentiability at 1: $-6a=b$ and $-3a-2=a^2+b$, so $a^2-3a+2=0$, $a=2$, $b=-12$.
$f(x)=-6x^2-2$ ($x<1$), $4-12x$ ($x\ge1$); it meets $y=-20$ at $x=-\sqrt3$ and $x=2$.
Area $=\displaystyle\int_{-\sqrt3}^{1}(18-6x^2)\,dx+\int_1^2(24-12x)\,dx=(16+12\sqrt3)+6=22+12\sqrt3$.
$\alpha+\beta=34$.

questions.text: If B is magnetic field and $\mu_0$ is permeability of free space, then the dimensions of $(B/\mu_0)$ is
questions.sol:
From $B=\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}$, $\dfrac{B}{\mu_0}=\dfrac{I}{2\pi r}$ has the dimensions of current per length.
$[B/\mu_0]=\mathrm{L^{-1}A}$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : In a vernier callipers, one vernier scale division is always smaller than one main scale division.
Statement II : The vernier constant is given by one main scale division multiplied by the number of vernier scale divisions.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
In a vernier callipers, $N$ vernier divisions equal $(N-1)$ main scale divisions, so one VSD is smaller than one MSD: Statement I is true.
The vernier constant is $1\text{ MSD}-1\text{ VSD}=\dfrac{1\text{ MSD}}{N}$, i.e. one MSD divided (not multiplied) by the number of vernier divisions: Statement II is false.

questions.text: A bob of mass m is suspended at a point O by a light string of length $l$ and left to perform vertical motion (circular) as shown in figure. Initially, by applying horizontal velocity $v_0$ at the point 'A', the string becomes slack when, the bob reaches at the point 'D'. The ratio of the kinetic energy of the bob at the points B and C is __________.
questions.sol:
At D (the top) the string just becomes slack, so $T=0$: $mg=\dfrac{mv_D^2}{l}$ and $K_D=\dfrac{mgl}{2}$.
Heights above A: B is at $l(1-\cos60^\circ)=\dfrac l2$, C is at $l(1+\cos60^\circ)=\dfrac{3l}{2}$, D is at $2l$.
$K_B=K_D+mg\left(2l-\dfrac l2\right)=2mgl$ and $K_C=K_D+mg\left(2l-\dfrac{3l}{2}\right)=mgl$.
$K_B:K_C=2$.

questions.text: A uniform circular disc of radius 'R' and mass 'M' is rotating about an axis perpendicular to its plane and passing through its centre. A small circular part of radius $R/2$ is removed from the original disc as shown in the figure. Find the moment of inertia of the remaining part of the original disc about the axis as given above.
questions.sol:
The removed disc has mass $\dfrac M4$ (area ratio $\dfrac14$) and its centre is $\dfrac R2$ from the axis.
Its moment of inertia about the axis: $\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac M4\left(\dfrac R2\right)^2+\dfrac M4\left(\dfrac R2\right)^2=\dfrac{3}{32}MR^2$.
Remaining: $\dfrac12MR^2-\dfrac3{32}MR^2=\dfrac{13}{32}MR^2$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text: A small point of mass m is placed at a distance 2R from the centre 'O' of a big uniform solid sphere of mass M and radius R. The gravitational force on 'm' due to M is $F_1$. A spherical part of radius $R/3$ is removed from the big sphere as shown in the figure and the gravitational force on m due to remaining part of M is found to be $F_2$. The value of ratio $F_1 : F_2$ is
questions.sol:
$F_1=\dfrac{GMm}{4R^2}$.
The removed sphere has mass $\dfrac{M}{27}$ and (as drawn) touches the surface on the side of m, so its centre is $\dfrac{2R}{3}$ from O and $\dfrac{4R}{3}$ from m.
Its pull: $\dfrac{G(M/27)m}{16R^2/9}=\dfrac{GMm}{48R^2}$.
$F_2=\dfrac{GMm}{R^2}\left(\dfrac14-\dfrac1{48}\right)=\dfrac{11}{48}\dfrac{GMm}{R^2}$, so $F_1:F_2=12:11$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two spherical bodies of same materials having radii 0.2 m and 0.8 m are placed in same atmosphere. The temperature of the smaller body is 800 K and temperature of the bigger body is 400 K. If the energy radiated from the smaller body is E, the energy radiated from the bigger body is (assume, effect of the surrounding temperature to be negligible),
questions.sol:
Stefan's law: radiated power $\propto AT^4\propto r^2T^4$ (same emissivity).
Ratio (bigger/smaller) $=\left(\dfrac{0.8}{0.2}\right)^2\left(\dfrac{400}{800}\right)^4=16\times\dfrac1{16}=1$.
So the bigger body radiates E.

questions.text:
An amount of ice of mass $10^{-3}$ kg and temperature $-10^\circ$C is transformed to vapour of temperature $110^\circ$C by applying heat. The total amount of work required for this conversion is,
(Take, specific heat of ice $=2100$ J kg$^{-1}$K$^{-1}$, specific heat of water $=4180$ J kg$^{-1}$K$^{-1}$, specific heat of steam $=1920$ J kg$^{-1}$K$^{-1}$, Latent heat of ice $=3.35\times10^5$ J kg$^{-1}$ and Latent heat of steam $=2.25\times10^6$ J kg$^{-1}$)
questions.sol:
Per kg: ice $-10\to0^\circ$C: $21000$; melting: $335000$; water $0\to100^\circ$C: $418000$; boiling: $2250000$; steam $100\to110^\circ$C: $19200$ (all in J).
Total per kg $=3043200$ J, so for $10^{-3}$ kg the energy needed is about $3043$ J.

questions.text: A closed organ and an open organ tube are filled by two different gases having same bulk modulus but different densities $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$, respectively. The frequency of 9$^{\text{th}}$ harmonic of closed tube is identical with 4$^{\text{th}}$ harmonic of open tube. If the length of the closed tube is 10 cm and the density ratio of the gases is $\rho_1 : \rho_2=1 : 16$, then the length of the open tube is :
questions.sol:
Speed of sound $v=\sqrt{B/\rho}$, so $\dfrac{v_1}{v_2}=\sqrt{\dfrac{\rho_2}{\rho_1}}=4$.
$\dfrac{9v_1}{4L_1}=\dfrac{4v_2}{2L_2} \Rightarrow L_2=\dfrac{8L_1v_2}{9v_1}=\dfrac{8\times10}{9\times4}=\dfrac{20}{9}$ cm.

questions.text: A parallel-plate capacitor of capacitance 40 $\mu$F is connected to a 100 V power supply. Now the intermediate space between the plates is filled with a dielectric material of dielectric constant K = 2. Due to the introduction of dielectric material, the extra charge and the change in the electrostatic energy in the capacitor, respectively, are
questions.sol:
The supply stays connected, so V is fixed and C doubles to $80\ \mu$F.
Extra charge $=(80-40)\times10^{-6}\times100=4\times10^{-3}$ C $=4$ mC.
Change in energy $=\dfrac12(80-40)\times10^{-6}\times100^2=0.2$ J.

questions.text:
An electron is made to enter symmetrically between two parallel and equally but oppositely charged metal plates, each of 10 cm length. The electron emerges out of the electric field region with a horizontal component of velocity $10^6$ m/s. If the magnitude of the electric field between the plates is 9.1 V/cm, then the vertical component of velocity of electron is
(mass of electron $=9.1\times10^{-31}$ kg and charge of electron $=1.6\times10^{-19}$ C)
questions.sol:
$E=9.1$ V/cm $=910$ V/m; $a=\dfrac{eE}{m}=\dfrac{1.6\times10^{-19}\times910}{9.1\times10^{-31}}=1.6\times10^{14}$ m/s$^2$.
Time between the plates $t=\dfrac{0.1}{10^6}=10^{-7}$ s.
$v_y=at=1.6\times10^7=16\times10^6$ m/s.

questions.text: A line charge of length $\dfrac{\text{'a'}}{2}$ is kept at the center of an edge BC of a cube ABCDEFGH having edge length 'a' as shown in the figure. If the density of line charge is $\lambda$ C per unit length, then the total electric flux through all the faces of the cube will be __________. (Take, $\epsilon_0$ as the free space permittivity)
questions.sol:
The charge $\dfrac{\lambda a}{2}$ lies on an edge, which is shared by four identical cubes; by symmetry this cube receives a quarter of the total flux.
Flux $=\dfrac14\cdot\dfrac{\lambda a/2}{\epsilon_0}=\dfrac{\lambda a}{8\epsilon_0}$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement-I : The equivalent emf of two nonideal batteries connected in parallel is smaller than either of the two emfs.
Statement-II : The equivalent internal resistance of two nonideal batteries connected in parallel is smaller than the internal resistance of either of the two batteries.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false
Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false
Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true
questions.sol:
$\varepsilon_{eq}=\dfrac{\varepsilon_1r_2+\varepsilon_2r_1}{r_1+r_2}$, a weighted mean, which lies between $\varepsilon_1$ and $\varepsilon_2$: Statement-I is false.
$r_{eq}=\dfrac{r_1r_2}{r_1+r_2}$ is smaller than both $r_1$ and $r_2$: Statement-II is true.

questions.text: Sliding contact of a potentiometer is in the middle of the potentiometer wire having resistance $R_p=1\ \Omega$ as shown in the figure. An external resistance of $R_e=2\ \Omega$ is connected via the sliding contact. The electric current in the circuit is :
questions.sol:
The 0.9 V cell is across the whole wire. $R_e$ is connected between one end and the midpoint, so it is in parallel with half the wire ($0.5\ \Omega$): $\dfrac{2\times0.5}{2.5}=0.4\ \Omega$.
This is in series with the other half: total $0.9\ \Omega$.
Current $=\dfrac{0.9}{0.9}=1.0$ A.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion-(A) : If Young's double slit experiment is performed in an optically denser medium than air, then the consecutive fringes come closer.
Reason-(R) : The speed of light reduces in an optically denser medium than air while its frequency does not change.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.sol:
In a denser medium the speed falls to $c/n$ while the frequency stays the same, so the wavelength becomes $\lambda/n$.
Fringe width $\beta=\dfrac{\lambda D}{d}$ therefore decreases by the factor $n$: fringes come closer.
Both are true and (R) explains (A).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Given is a thin convex lens of glass (refractive index $\mu$) and each side having radius of curvature R. One side is polished for complete reflection. At what distance from the lens, an object be placed on the optic axis so that the image gets formed on the object itself ?
questions.sol:
The silvered lens acts as a mirror of power $P=2P_L+P_M$, with $P_L=(\mu-1)\dfrac2R$ and $P_M=\dfrac2R$.
$P=\dfrac{4(\mu-1)+2}{R}=\dfrac{2(2\mu-1)}{R}$, so the equivalent mirror has focal length $\dfrac{R}{2(2\mu-1)}$.
The image coincides with the object at the centre of curvature, i.e. at $2f=\dfrac{R}{2\mu-1}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In the diagram given below, there are three lenses formed. Considering negligible thickness of each of them as compared to $|R_1|$ and $|R_2|$, i.e., the radii of curvature for upper and lower surfaces of the glass lens, the power of the combination is
questions.sol:
Both glass surfaces curve downwards (centres of curvature above). Take light travelling downwards.
Upper water lens (flat top, surface $R_1$ below): $P_1=\left(\dfrac43-1\right)\dfrac1{|R_1|}=\dfrac{1}{3|R_1|}$.
Glass lens: $P_2=\left(\dfrac32-1\right)\left(-\dfrac1{|R_1|}+\dfrac1{|R_2|}\right)$.
Lower water lens (surface $R_2$ above, flat bottom): $P_3=\left(\dfrac43-1\right)\left(-\dfrac1{|R_2|}\right)$.
Sum: $-\dfrac{1}{6|R_1|}+\dfrac1{6|R_2|}=-\dfrac16\left(\dfrac1{|R_1|}-\dfrac1{|R_2|}\right)$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The work functions of cesium (Cs) and lithium (Li) metals are 1.9 eV and 2.5 eV, respectively. If we incident a light of wavelength 550 nm on these two metal surfaces, then photo-electric effect is possible for the case of
questions.sol:
Photon energy $=\dfrac{1240}{550}\approx2.25$ eV.
This exceeds 1.9 eV (Cs) but not 2.5 eV (Li), so emission occurs from Cs only.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: An electron in the ground state of the hydrogen atom has the orbital radius of $5.3\times10^{-11}$ m while that for the electron in third excited state is $8.48\times10^{-10}$ m. The ratio of the de Broglie wavelengths of electron in the ground state to that in the excited state is
questions.note: With $\lambda\propto n$, the ratio ground : excited is strictly $1:4$; NTA's final key gives option (2), 4, i.e. the ratio of the larger to the smaller wavelength.
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{r_n}{r_1}=\dfrac{8.48\times10^{-10}}{5.3\times10^{-11}}=16=n^2$, so $n=4$ (the third excited state).
Bohr's condition $2\pi r_n=n\lambda_n$ gives $\lambda_n=\dfrac{2\pi r_n}{n}\propto n$.
So the two wavelengths differ by a factor of 4 (the excited-state wavelength is 4 times the ground-state one); the final key takes this factor, 4, as the answer.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Which of the following circuits represents a forward biased diode ?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A diode is forward biased when its p-side (the triangle end) is at a higher potential than its n-side (the bar).
(A): p at $-10$ V, n at 0 V: reverse. (B): $-10$ V $>-15$ V: forward. (C): 4 V $>$ 2 V: forward.
(D): the diode points the other way; p at $-10$ V, n at $-5$ V: reverse. (E): p at 2 V, n earthed: forward.
Answer: (B), (C) and (E).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The position vectors of two 1 kg particles, (A) and (B), are given by $\vec{r}_A=\left(\alpha_1t^2\hat{i}+\alpha_2t\hat{j}+\alpha_3t\hat{k}\right)$ m and $\vec{r}_B=\left(\beta_1t\hat{i}+\beta_2t^2\hat{j}+\beta_3t\hat{k}\right)$ m, respectively; ($\alpha_1=1$ m/s$^2$, $\alpha_2=3n$ m/s, $\alpha_3=2$ m/s, $\beta_1=2$ m/s, $\beta_2=-1$ m/s$^2$, $\beta_3=4p$ m/s), where t is time, n and p are constants. At $t=1$ s, $\left|\vec{V}_A\right|=\left|\vec{V}_B\right|$ and velocities $\vec{V}_A$ and $\vec{V}_B$ of the particles are orthogonal to each other. At $t=1$ s, the magnitude of angular momentum of particle (A) with respect to the position of particle (B) is $\sqrt{L}$ kg m$^2$s$^{-1}$. The value of L is __________.
questions.sol:
At $t=1$: $\vec V_A=(2, 3n, 2)$, $\vec V_B=(2, -2, 4p)$.
Equal speeds: $9n^2=16p^2$. Orthogonal: $4-6n+8p=0$. With $3n=4p$ the second equation fails, so $3n=-4p$, giving $p=-\dfrac14$, $n=\dfrac13$.
$\vec r_A=(1, 1, 2)$, $\vec r_B=(2, -1, -1)$, $\vec V_A=(2, 1, 2)$.
$\vec L=(\vec r_A-\vec r_B)\times m\vec V_A=(-1, 2, 3)\times(2, 1, 2)=(1, 8, -5)$; $|\vec L|^2=90$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text:
A particle is projected at an angle of $30^\circ$ from horizontal at a speed of 60 m/s. The height traversed by the particle in the first second is $h_0$ and height traversed in the last second, before it reaches the maximum height, is $h_1$. The ratio $h_0 : h_1$ is __________.
[Take, $g=10$ m/s$^2$]
questions.sol:
Vertical component $u_y=60\sin30^\circ=30$ m/s; time to the top $=3$ s.
$h_0=30(1)-5(1)^2=25$ m.
The last second before the top is the reverse of a 1 s fall from rest: $h_1=\dfrac12g(1)^2=5$ m.
$h_0:h_1=5$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two soap bubbles of radius 2 cm and 4 cm, respectively, are in contact with each other. The radius of curvature of the common surface, in cm, is __________.
questions.sol:
The excess pressures are $\dfrac{4T}{r_1}$ and $\dfrac{4T}{r_2}$; their difference acts across the common film: $\dfrac{4T}{r}=\dfrac{4T}{r_1}-\dfrac{4T}{r_2}$.
$r=\dfrac{r_1r_2}{r_2-r_1}=\dfrac{2\times4}{2}=4$ cm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Three conductors of same length having thermal conductivity $k_1$, $k_2$ and $k_3$ are connected as shown in figure.
Area of cross sections of 1$^{\text{st}}$ and 2$^{\text{nd}}$ conductor are same and for 3$^{\text{rd}}$ conductor it is double of the 1$^{\text{st}}$ conductor. The temperatures are given in the figure. In steady state condition, the value of $\theta$ is __________ $^\circ$C.
(Given : $k_1=60$ J s$^{-1}$m$^{-1}$K$^{-1}$, $k_2=120$ J s$^{-1}$m$^{-1}$K$^{-1}$, $k_3=135$ J s$^{-1}$m$^{-1}$K$^{-1}$)
questions.sol:
Conductors 1 and 2 are in parallel between 100$^\circ$C and $\theta$; conductor 3 (area $2A$) carries the same heat current from $\theta$ to 0$^\circ$C.
$(k_1+k_2)A(100-\theta)=k_3(2A)\theta \Rightarrow 180(100-\theta)=270\theta$.
$\theta=40^\circ$C.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The driver sitting inside a parked car is watching vehicles approaching from behind with the help of his side view mirror, which is a convex mirror with radius of curvature R = 2 m. Another car approaches him from behind with a uniform speed of 90 km/hr. When the car is at a distance of 24 m from him, the magnitude of the acceleration of the image of the car in the side view mirror is 'a'. The value of 100a is __________ m/s$^2$.
questions.sol:
$f=+1$ m, $u=-24$ m, $\dfrac{du}{dt}=25$ m/s (constant).
$v=\dfrac{uf}{u-f}$, so $\dfrac{dv}{dt}=-\dfrac{f^2}{(u-f)^2}\dfrac{du}{dt}$ and $\dfrac{d^2v}{dt^2}=\dfrac{2f^2}{(u-f)^3}\left(\dfrac{du}{dt}\right)^2$.
$|a|=\dfrac{2\times1\times625}{25^3}=0.08$ m/s$^2$, so $100a=8$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Radius of the first excited state of Helium ion is given as :
$a_0\rightarrow$ radius of first stationary state of hydrogen atom.
questions.sol:
For a hydrogen-like ion $r_n=\dfrac{n^2}{Z}a_0$.
$\mathrm{He^+}$: $Z=2$; first excited state $n=2$: $r=\dfrac{4}{2}a_0=2a_0$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: A liquid when kept inside a thermally insulated closed vessel at $25^\circ$C was mechanically stirred from outside. What will be the correct option for the following thermodynamic parameters ?
questions.sol:
The vessel is insulated, so $q=0$.
Stirring does work on the liquid: $w>0$.
$\Delta U=q+w=w>0$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Arrange the following solutions in order of their increasing boiling points.
(i) $10^{-4}$ M NaCl
(ii) $10^{-4}$ M Urea
(iii) $10^{-3}$ M NaCl
(iv) $10^{-2}$ M NaCl
questions.sol:
Boiling-point elevation is proportional to $iC$ (dilute solutions).
Urea: $1\times10^{-4}$; NaCl: $2\times10^{-4}$, $2\times10^{-3}$, $2\times10^{-2}$.
Order: (ii) < (i) < (iii) < (iv).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: A vessel at 1000 K contains $\mathrm{CO_2}$ with a pressure of 0.5 atm. Some of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ is converted into CO on addition of graphite. If total pressure at equilibrium is 0.8 atm, then $K_p$ is :
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{CO_2(g)+C(s)\rightleftharpoons2CO(g)}$. If $x$ atm of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ reacts: $(0.5-x)+2x=0.8$, so $x=0.3$.
$p_{\mathrm{CO_2}}=0.2$ atm, $p_{\mathrm{CO}}=0.6$ atm.
$K_p=\dfrac{0.6^2}{0.2}=1.8$ atm.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
A solution of aluminium chloride is electrolysed for 30 minutes using a current of 2A. The amount of the aluminium deposited at the cathode is __________.
[Given : molar mass of aluminium and chlorine are 27 g mol$^{-1}$ and 35.5 g mol$^{-1}$ respectively. Faraday constant $=96500$ C mol$^{-1}$]
questions.sol:
Charge $=2\times1800=3600$ C $=\dfrac{3600}{96500}=0.0373$ mol of electrons.
$\mathrm{Al^{3+}+3e^-\rightarrow Al}$: moles of Al $=0.01244$.
Mass $=0.01244\times27\approx0.336$ g.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which of the following electrolyte can be used to obtain $\mathrm{H_2S_2O_8}$ by the process of electrolysis ?
options: Acidified dilute solution of sodium sulphate.
questions.sol:
In dilute sulphuric acid (or sulphate solutions) water is oxidised at the anode and $\mathrm{O_2}$ is evolved.
At high concentration of sulphuric acid, $\mathrm{HSO_4^-}$ is oxidised instead: $\mathrm{2HSO_4^-\rightarrow H_2S_2O_8+2e^-}$ (peroxodisulphuric acid).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which of the following statement is not true for radioactive decay ?
options: Half life is ln 2 times of $\dfrac{1}{\text{rate constant}}$.
Decay constant does not depend upon temperature.
Amount of radioactive substance remained after three half lives is $\dfrac{1}{8}$ th of original amount.
Decay constant increases with increase in temperature.
questions.sol:
Radioactive decay is first order: $t_{1/2}=\dfrac{\ln2}{k}$ and after three half-lives $\left(\dfrac12\right)^3=\dfrac18$ remains.
It is a nuclear process, so the decay constant does not depend on temperature.
The false statement is "decay constant increases with increase in temperature".
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which of the following electronegativity order is incorrect ?
questions.sol:
Pauling values: Mg 1.2, Al 1.5, Be 1.5, B 2.0, Si 1.8, C 2.5, S 2.5, N 3.0, Cl 3.0, O 3.5, F 4.0.
Mg is less electronegative than Al, so "Al < Mg < B < N" is incorrect; the other orders hold.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-IList-II
(A) $\mathrm{Al^{3+}<Mg^{2+}<Na^+<F^-}$(I) Ionisation Enthalpy
(B) B < C < O < N(II) Metallic character
(C) B < Al < Mg < K(III) Electronegativity
(D) Si < P < S < Cl(IV) Ionic radii
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
(A) Isoelectronic ions: radius falls as nuclear charge rises, so $\mathrm{Al^{3+}<Mg^{2+}<Na^+<F^-}$ is ionic radii (IV).
(B) B < C < O < N is first ionisation enthalpy (N above O because of its half-filled 2p) (I).
(C) B < Al < Mg < K is metallic character (II).
(D) Si < P < S < Cl is electronegativity (III).
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text:
Lanthanoid ions with $4f^7$ configuration are :
(A) $\mathrm{Eu^{2+}}$
(B) $\mathrm{Gd^{3+}}$
(C) $\mathrm{Eu^{3+}}$
(D) $\mathrm{Tb^{3+}}$
(E) $\mathrm{Sm^{2+}}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Eu is $[\mathrm{Xe}]4f^76s^2$, so $\mathrm{Eu^{2+}}$ is $4f^7$; Gd is $[\mathrm{Xe}]4f^75d^16s^2$, so $\mathrm{Gd^{3+}}$ is $4f^7$.
$\mathrm{Eu^{3+}}$ and $\mathrm{Sm^{2+}}$ are $4f^6$; $\mathrm{Tb^{3+}}$ is $4f^8$.
Answer: (A) and (B) only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: From the magnetic behaviour of $\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}$ (paramagnetic) and $\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}$ (diamagnetic), choose the correct geometry and oxidation state.
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}$: $\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$ ($3d^8$); weak-field $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ gives $sp^3$ with two unpaired electrons: tetrahedral, paramagnetic.
$\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}$: Ni(0), $3d^{10}$ after pairing by CO; $sp^3$: tetrahedral, diamagnetic.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: In which of the following complexes the CFSE, $\Delta_o$ will be equal to zero ?
questions.sol:
CFSE is zero for a high-spin $d^5$ ion ($t_{2g}^3e_g^2$: $3(-0.4)+2(0.6)=0$).
$\mathrm{K_3[Fe(SCN)_6]}$: $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ ($d^5$) with the weak-field ligand $\mathrm{SCN^-}$, high spin, so CFSE $=0$.
$\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ ($d^6$) complexes and low-spin $\mathrm{[Fe(en)_3]^{3+}}$ have non-zero CFSE.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The IUPAC name of the following compound is :
questions.note: NTA's final key gives option (4). By current IUPAC rules the compound, $\mathrm{HOOC-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_2-CH(CH_3)-COOCH_3}$, would be named 6-methoxy-2,5-dimethyl-6-oxohexanoic acid; of the options given, (4) is the one that keeps the carboxylic acid as the principal group with the ester as a substituent.
questions.sol:
The carboxylic acid ranks above the ester, so the name ends in "-oic acid" and the ester is cited as a substituent.
Options (1) and (3) treat the ester as the principal group, and option (2) names the compound as a hexane, so they are wrong.
The final key accepts option (4), 6-methoxycarbonyl-2,5-dimethylhexanoic acid.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text: How many different stereoisomers are possible for the given molecule ?
questions.sol:
Pent-3-en-2-ol, $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)CH=CHCH_3}$, has one chiral carbon (C-2) and a C=C bond that can be cis or trans.
Number of stereoisomers $=2\times2=4$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text:
The incorrect statements regarding geometrical isomerism are :
(A) Propene shows geometrical isomerism.
(B) Trans isomer has identical atoms/groups on the opposite sides of the double bond.
(C) Cis-but-2-ene has higher dipole moment than trans-but-2-ene.
(D) 2-methylbut-2-ene shows two geometrical isomers.
(E) Trans-isomer has lower melting point than cis isomer.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
(A) Propene has two H atoms on one doubly bonded carbon: no geometrical isomers. Incorrect.
(B) and (C) are correct.
(D) 2-methylbut-2-ene has two methyl groups on C-2: no geometrical isomers. Incorrect.
(E) The trans isomer packs better and usually melts higher. Incorrect.
Answer: (A), (D) and (E).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : One mole of propyne reacts with excess of sodium to liberate half a mole of $\mathrm{H_2}$ gas.
Statement II : Four g of propyne reacts with $\mathrm{NaNH_2}$ to liberate $\mathrm{NH_3}$ gas which occupies 224 mL at STP.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
Propyne has one acidic hydrogen: $\mathrm{CH_3C\equiv CH+Na\rightarrow CH_3C\equiv CNa+\tfrac12H_2}$, so Statement I is correct.
4 g of propyne is 0.1 mol and gives 0.1 mol $\mathrm{NH_3}$, i.e. 2240 mL at STP, not 224 mL: Statement II is incorrect.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : $\mathrm{CH_3-O-CH_2-Cl}$ will undergo $\mathrm{S_N1}$ reaction though it is a primary halide.
Statement II : $\mathrm{CH_3-\overset{CH_3}{\underset{CH_3}{C}}-CH_2-Cl}$ will not undergo $\mathrm{S_N2}$ reaction very easily though it is a primary halide.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
Statement I: the carbocation $\mathrm{CH_3-O-\overset{+}{C}H_2}$ is stabilised by resonance with the oxygen lone pair, so this primary halide reacts by $\mathrm{S_N1}$. Correct.
Statement II: in neopentyl chloride the bulky tert-butyl group blocks back-side attack, so $\mathrm{S_N2}$ is very slow. Correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The products formed in the following reaction sequence are :
questions.sol:
(i) $\mathrm{NO_2}$ is meta-directing: bromination gives 3-bromonitrobenzene.
(ii) Sn/HCl reduces it to 3-bromoaniline.
(iii) Diazotisation gives the 3-bromobenzenediazonium salt.
(iv) Ethanol reduces the diazonium salt to bromobenzene and is itself oxidised to ethanal: $\mathrm{ArN_2^+Cl^-+CH_3CH_2OH\rightarrow ArH+N_2+CH_3CHO+HCl}$.
Products: bromobenzene and $\mathrm{CH_3CHO}$, option (2).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which of the following acids is a vitamin ?
questions.sol:
Ascorbic acid is vitamin C.
Aspartic acid is an amino acid, adipic acid is hexanedioic acid and saccharic acid is the dicarboxylic acid from oxidation of glucose; none of them is a vitamin.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The compounds which give positive Fehling's test are :
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Fehling's solution is reduced by aliphatic aldehydes and by $\alpha$-hydroxy ketones, but not by aromatic aldehydes or ordinary ketones.
(A) benzaldehyde: negative. (B) acetophenone: negative.
(C) fructose (an $\alpha$-hydroxy ketone), (D) ethanal and (E) phenylethanal (the CHO is on an $\mathrm{sp^3}$ carbon): positive.
Answer: (C), (D) and (E).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Some $\mathrm{CO_2}$ gas was kept in a sealed container at a pressure of 1 atm and at 273 K. This entire amount of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ gas was later passed through an aqueous solution of $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}$. The excess unreacted $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}$ was later neutralized with 0.1 M of 40 mL HCl. If the volume of the sealed container of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ was x, then x is __________ cm$^3$ (nearest integer).
[Given : The entire amount of $\mathrm{CO_2(g)}$ reacted with exactly half the initial amount of $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}$ present in the aqueous solution.]
questions.sol:
HCl used $=0.1\times0.040=4\times10^{-3}$ mol, which neutralises $2\times10^{-3}$ mol of $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}$.
This excess is half the original amount, so the other half, $2\times10^{-3}$ mol, reacted with $\mathrm{CO_2}$ ($\mathrm{CO_2+Ca(OH)_2\rightarrow CaCO_3+H_2O}$): $n(\mathrm{CO_2})=2\times10^{-3}$ mol.
At 1 atm and 273 K: $V=2\times10^{-3}\times22400=44.8\ \mathrm{cm^3}\approx45$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The number of molecules/ions that show linear geometry among the following is __________.
$\mathrm{SO_2}$, $\mathrm{BeCl_2}$, $\mathrm{CO_2}$, $\mathrm{N_3^-}$, $\mathrm{NO_2}$, $\mathrm{F_2O}$, $\mathrm{XeF_2}$, $\mathrm{NO_2^+}$, $\mathrm{I_3^-}$, $\mathrm{O_3}$
questions.sol:
Linear: $\mathrm{BeCl_2}$, $\mathrm{CO_2}$, $\mathrm{N_3^-}$, $\mathrm{NO_2^+}$ (two bonding domains, no lone pairs on the centre) and $\mathrm{XeF_2}$, $\mathrm{I_3^-}$ (three lone pairs in the equatorial plane).
Bent: $\mathrm{SO_2}$, $\mathrm{NO_2}$, $\mathrm{F_2O}$, $\mathrm{O_3}$.
Count $=6$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
$\mathrm{A\rightarrow B}$
The molecule A changes into its isomeric form B by following a first order kinetics at a temperature of 1000 K. If the energy barrier with respect to reactant energy for such isomeric transformation is 191.48 kJ mol$^{-1}$ and the frequency factor is $10^{20}$, the time required for 50% molecules of A to become B is __________ picoseconds (nearest integer). [R = 8.314 J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$]
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
In Carius method for estimation of halogens, 180 mg of an organic compound produced 143.5 mg of AgCl. The percentage composition of chlorine in the compound is __________%.
(Given : molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ of Ag : 108, Cl : 35.5)
questions.sol:
Mass of Cl $=143.5\times\dfrac{35.5}{143.5}=35.5$ mg.
Percentage $=\dfrac{35.5}{180}\times100\approx19.7\%$, i.e. 20.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text:
Consider the following sequence of reactions :
Molar mass of the product formed (A) is __________ g mol$^{-1}$.
questions.sol:
Sn/HCl reduces nitrobenzene to aniline; $\mathrm{NaNO_2}$/HCl at 0$^\circ$C gives benzenediazonium chloride; $\mathrm{Cu_2Cl_2}$ (Sandmeyer) gives chlorobenzene.
Na in dry ether (Fittig reaction) couples two aryl groups: A is biphenyl, $\mathrm{C_{12}H_{10}}$.
Molar mass $=144+10=154$ g mol$^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
